claims.author: sedited
claims.question: Whether a failure to serialize should be categorized as a Result under the proposed strategy.
claims.quote: Should a failure to serialize be what you call here a Result?

status_by.quote: Yes. Well, it depends on the contract of the function... Such a function would return std::optional<Block>, for example.

claims.status_note: author explained that parsing untrusted network data fits into returning an optional/Result rather than throwing runtime errors.

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: What category unchecked exceptions like bad_alloc or standard library length errors and invalid arguments fit into under the proposal.
claims.quote: Some of the code we call in the standard library does throw on length errors and invalid arguments. In what category do those fit in?

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: Exceptions introduce unpredictable side-effects and invisible non-local control flow contrary to recent project direction.
claims.quote: Approach NACK, instead of presenting your personal opinion as the only way forward, try gathering info first on the project's needs

status_by.quote: An exception is an unannounced return value, it's a surprise, a side-effect: a lie.

claims.status_note: l0rinc pushed back arguing exceptions introduce non-local invisible control flow and calling throwing constructors a recipe for disaster.

claims.author: furszy
claims.harm: Ungraceful process aborts on defects prevent graceful flushing and can leave the wallet database in an inconsistent or unrecoverable state, risking funds.
claims.quote: There are multiple examples where abrupt terminations can cause the wallet to enter an inconsistent/unrecoverable state, which puts users' funds at risk.

status_by.quote: Only the affected subsystem should avoid flushing to disk. All others should be allowed to shut down gracefully.

claims.status_note: furszy pushed back, arguing that a defect in one subsystem does not justify aborting without allowing other subsystems like the wallet to flush safely.

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Contradicts established codebase patterns like util::Expected and util::Result, introducing technical debt and worse error handling semantics.
claims.quote: NACK, this isn't a problem that needs a 750 word essay to address... and the essay provided doesn't reflect existing practice (eg util/expected.h or util/result.h) so if merged would introduce signifi

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: Broad exception propagation forces reviewers to audit all calling threads and destructors for deadlock hazards during shutdown.
claims.quote: If exceptions were used more broadly, reviewers must always implicitly consider all calling threads for all functions and waste review cycles on that

claims.author: willcl-ark
claims.question: Whether the author considered the LLVM-style explicit-error-handling model and why exceptions are considered more appropriate for Bitcoin Core.
claims.quote: I'd be interested to know whether you considered the LLVM-style approach in formulating this, and why you consider your approach as more appropriate for our project?

status_by.quote: The two reasons why exceptions are preferred for Bitcoin Core specifically are: A clear separation between Result and Error... The optimization for the success path.

claims.status_note: author replied detailing reasons why exceptions are preferred for Bitcoin Core over LLVM's approach.

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.harm: A global abort-on-defect directive breaks existing resilience patterns where non-consensus modules like P2P or RPC can handle bugs without node crashes.
claims.quote: in p2p code that is triggerable remotely it is often best practice to add a debug-only Assume() and just abort the processing of the message, but not the entire program

status_by.quote: it is completely unacceptable to sacrifice any locally desired functional outcome in favor of nicer code or project-wide consistency

claims.status_note: mzumsande pushed back, reiterating that a project-wide policy dictating defect handling outcomes is unacceptable given remote crash risks and defensive programming needs.

claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: The document creates internally contradictory documentation with existing utilities and belongs in doc/developer-notes.md rather than as a top-level document.
claims.quote: it can absolutely not be merged in its current form, while ignoring the review feedback above. Merging it would create internally contradictory documentation. Also, doc/error-handling.md is the wrong
claims.status_note: author acknowledged refinement is needed in c:5461417690 but deferred actionable updates.
